newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS BEAT ISLANDERS 3-1.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS BEAT ISLANDERS 3-1.

text.p: Stephane Richer had a goal and an assist and Jocelyn Thibault made 26 saves as the Montreal Canadiens extended their unbeaten streak to six games with a 3-1 triumph over the New York Islanders on Saturday.
Darcy Tucker and Vincent Damphousse had the other goals and rookie Sebastien Bordeleau had two assists for the Canadiens.
"Young guys like me, Tucker and (Craig) Rivet, we don't want to go back to the minors," Bordeleau said. "We're getting our chance to play and we want to stay here."
In Boston, Ray Bourque scored with 36 seconds left to lift the Boston Bruins to their first win over a Central Division opponent this season, 3-2 over the Dallas Stars.
Bourque was at the top of the left faceoff circle and beat goaltender Roman Turek with a one-timer for his fourth goal.
Turek made 22 saves and lost for the first time in three NHL decisions, and the Stars have lost four of their last five games.

At Colorado, Trent Klatt and Mikael Renberg scored in the final eight minutes of regulation and the Philadelphia Flyers extended their unbeaten streak to 16 games by rallying for a 4-4 tie with the Colorado Avalanche in a battle of the NHL's top two teams.
The Avalanche appeared headed for their sixth straight win as they built a 4-1 lead early in the second period.
But Philadelphia climbed within two on Dale Hawerchuk's goal with 12:08 to go in the second period.
The Flyers cut the margin to one at 12:01 and tied it two minutes later.
In Hartford, Steve Konowalchuk's goal with 4:14 remaining lifted the Washington Capitals into a 1-1 tie with the Hartford Whalers.

Joe Reekie grabbed a loose puck in the neutral zone and sent it to former Whaler Andrei Nikolishin, who left a touch pass for Peter Bondra. Bondra carried over the Hartford blue line and passed to Konowalchuk, whose wrist shot tipped off goaltender Jason Muzzatti's glove and into the net.
Mark Janssens had the only goal for Hartford.
In New York, Niklas Sundstrom and Luc Robitaille each scored twice, and Wayne Gretzky had four assists in a five-goal second period as the New York Rangers beat the Ottawa Senators 6-4.
The Rangers stretched their home winning streak to five games behind Gretzky's 57th career four-assist game. Mike Richter made 35 saves to extend his personal unbeaten streak to 15 games (14-0-1).
In Pittsburg, Mario Lemieux scored twice and had three assists as the Pittsburgh Penguins ran their unbeaten streak to eight games with a 7-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Rookie Patrick Lalime made 28 saves to improve to 9-0-1 since his recall from the minors. Ron Francis added two goals and an assist for Pittsburgh.
Lemieux has points in nine straight games on 14 goals and 11 assists.
"The big guys were flying out there," Pittsburgh coach Eddie Johnston said. "We were fortunate to catch a club that didn't get in until four or five in the morning. We played a tired hockey club."
In Los Angeles, John Vanbiesbrouck made 28 saves for his second shutout of the season and Scott Mellanby had a goal and three assists as the Florida Panthers beat the Los Angeles Kings 5-0.
Rob Niedermayer added a goal and two assists and Gord Murphy scored Florida's final two goals.
In San Jose, Jonas Hoglund scored with 4:22 left to cap a three-goal third period as the Calgary Flames rallied for a 4-3 victory over the San Jose Sharks, snapping a four-game losing streak.
Ed Ward and Robert Reichel also scored in the third for the Flames.
In Vancouver, Mike Sillinger scored twice and Pavel Bure, Martin Gelinas and Gino Odjick each had a goal and an assist as the Vancouver Canucks routed the Toronto Maple Leafs, 7-3.
David Roberts picked up two assists for Vancouver, which won for just the second time in six games.
Mats Sundin scored his 25th and 26th goals for the Maple Leafs.
